Uvijek dodajte napust (bleed) na konačnu dimenziju datoteke jer ćete time olakšati kod rezanja na format i neće se pojavljivati bijeli obrub Napust neka iznosi 3mm preko ruba završenog formata osim ako nije drugačije definirano u uputi za grafičku priprema za taj proizvod.
Napusti se definiraju za sve četiri strane bez obzira na poziciju stranice (lijeva, desna), te vrstu uveza.
Stranice se šalju pojedinačno centrirane na izlazni format Može ih biti i više u jednom dokumentu, ali samo s oznakama reza, sve ostale oznake su suvišne.
Sav sadržaj treba biti barem 5mm od linije reza; kod nekih proizvoda je definirana sigurna zona (roza linija)
Kod pozadinskih boja ili slika, ukoliko idu do ruba proizvoda, tada ostavite napust.
Slike, grafike, tekst i linije
Svi rasterski elementi grafičke pripreme trebali bi biti oko:
30 dpi za XXL formate preko 12 m2 (jumbo plakati, megaboardi…),
60 do 100 dpi za formate A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 (plakati, posteri, pultevi, roll upovi, banneri…),
100 do 150 dpi za format A3 (manji plakati, slike…),
200 do 300 dpi za formate A4, A5 (katalozi, prospekti, vizitke…).
Logotipovi, tekstovi, linije i sl. trebaju biti u vektorskom obliku
Ako priprema sadrži tekst, sav tekst pretvoriti u krivulje ili poslati korišteni font za PC.

Datoteke neka budu u omjeru 1:1 za manje vizuale ili 1:10 za velike vizuale; ukoliko priprema nije u 1:1 mjerilu, tada je potrebno naglasiti u kojem je mjerilu napravljena i koja je finalna dimenzija.

Format datoteke
Preferiramo dostavu dokumenata u pdf ili tif formatu. Prihvaćamo i slijedeće formate datoteka za digitalni tisak: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Uz datoteku s grafičkom pripremom, molimo pošaljite i preview niže rezolucije (.jpg).

content.text: Jumbo posters are a very cheap and fast way to advertise your product, services and the company itself.
A quality jumbo poster design will surely attract the attention of potential buyers.
Jumbo posters are simple and functional because they can be set up as a permanent installation or for temporary advertising.
The most common jumbo poster size is 504x238 cm or 400x300cm
Jumbo posters are made on Blueback paper, i.e. paper with a blue back so that when pasting over existing posters the previous motifs do not show through.
For making jumbo posters we use only top-quality and durable materials.
Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).

content.text: Ploče su veoma pogodne za rezanje (oblikovanje) i izuzetno su lagane.

Nudimo i mogućnost konturnog rezanja odnosno izradu željenog oblika i formata.
AccaFoam dolazi u debljinama od 3mm, 5mm, 10mm

Prilikom stvaranja grafičkih priprema, nekoliko stvari trebate imati na umu kako bi kreirali ispravnu grafičku priprema stoga smo sastavili nekoliko savjeta i smjernica.
Ukoliko niste sigurni kako najbolje pripremiti dokument za naš tisak slobodno nas nazovite na telefon 098 9085 552 te ćemo rado pomoći svojim savjetima.

Izbjegavajte 4C za crnu boju; umjesto toga dovoljno je da je 100% K (crna).
Kada koristite specijalne boje (Pantone ili HKS) molimo vas da posebno napomenete kod narudžbe.
Provjerite da li su svi objekti koji se preklapaju ispravno podešeni (overprint).
Ako naručite datoteku u sivoj boji, tada preporučujemo da je siva stvorena u nijansama crne.
Bijela boja mora biti zasebna spot boja, obaveznog naziva “White_Ink“ (paziti na velika i mala slova), u overprintu i u top layeru.

Datoteke kreirajte u njihovoj stvarnoj konačnoj dimenziji sa napustima.

Uvijek dodajte napust (bleed) na konačnu dimenziju datoteke jer ćete time olakšati kod rezanja na format i neće se pojavljivati bijeli obrub Napust neka iznosi 3mm preko ruba završenog formata osim ako nije drugačije definirano u uputi za grafičku priprema za taj proizvod.
Napusti se definiraju za sve četiri strane bez obzira na poziciju stranice (lijeva, desna), te vrstu uveza.
Stranice se šalju pojedinačno centrirane na izlazni format Može ih biti i više u jednom dokumentu, ali samo s oznakama reza, sve ostale oznake su suvišne.
Sav sadržaj treba biti barem 5mm od linije reza; kod nekih proizvoda je definirana sigurna zona (roza linija)
Kod pozadinskih boja ili slika, ukoliko idu do ruba proizvoda, tada ostavite napust.

30 dpi za XXL formate preko 12 m2 (jumbo plakati, megaboardi…),
60 do 100 dpi za formate A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 (plakati, posteri, pultevi, roll upovi, banneri…),
100 do 150 dpi za format A3 (manji plakati, slike…),
200 do 300 dpi za formate A4, A5 (katalozi, prospekti, vizitke…).
Logotipovi, tekstovi, linije i sl. trebaju biti u vektorskom obliku
Ako priprema sadrži tekst, sav tekst pretvoriti u krivulje ili poslati korišteni font za PC.

Datoteke neka budu u omjeru 1:1 za manje vizuale ili 1:10 za velike vizuale; ukoliko priprema nije u 1:1 mjerilu, tada je potrebno naglasiti u kojem je mjerilu napravljena i koja je finalna dimenzija.
Linije trebaju biti debljine barem 0.125 pt
Molimo da linije prilagodite tako da budu vidljive kod tiska; ovisno na kojem materijalu se izrađuje shodno treba i podesiti debljinu-na zastavama veća debljina dok na letku tanja linija.

Preferiramo dostavu dokumenata u pdf ili tif formatu. Prihvaćamo i slijedeće formate datoteka za digitalni tisak: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Uz datoteku s grafičkom pripremom, molimo pošaljite i preview niže rezolucije (.jpg).

content.text: With a digital sublimation printer of a maximum width of 320cm we can produce a wide range of products such as bags, tablecloths, curtains, sunbed fabrics, flags, etc.
We make the products according to your finishing criteria and offer the following finishing methods:
Tunnel
Carabiner
Reinforcement strip
Rope
Ring
Silicone keder
For making the fabrics we use only top-quality and durable polyester materials of EU origin.
Depending on your wishes, our standard range includes the following materials:
Teleios Grande H6
The large-format textile printer is used for printing on polyester materials, mainly flags, textile banners, interior-decoration materials, or for various presentation systems.
It offers a wide range of colours and high saturation. Printing on textile is becoming increasingly popular due to its low weight, simple transport and installation.
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h.
HP Stitch S1000

The large-format sublimation textile printer is intended for professional production of printing on polyester materials. It is ideal for making flags, textile banners, interior-decoration graphics and various promotional and exhibition systems.
The HP Stitch S1000 offers an exceptionally wide colour range and high saturation, with precise colour management thanks to HP's advanced calibration technology.
We are able to print at a maximum width of up to 320 cm, at a speed of up to 220 m²/h, with top quality and colour fastness.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).

content.text: Dibond is an aluminium sandwich board, hardened with a polyethylene compound that prevents the deformations caused by weather conditions.

The boards are very suitable for cutting (shaping) and are extremely lightweight.

Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.

content.text: Ploče su veoma pogodne za rezanje (oblikovanje) i izuzetno su lagane.
Oslikavanje vršimo direktnim UV tiskom na ploču ili digitalnim solventnim ili UV printom na naljepnicu koju zatim kaširamo na Dibond ploču.
Nudimo i mogućnost konturnog rezanja odnosno izradu željenog oblika i formata.
Mimaki UJV 55-320
U mogućnosti smo izraditi tisak maksimalne širine 320cm brzinom od 177m2/h. Mimaki UJV55-320 je printer velikog formata maksimalne širine ispisa 320cm.

Omogućuje visoku kvalitetu otiska, brzi ispis te ekonomičnost, a glavna prednost UV printera je ta što nije potrebno laminirati otisak radi zaštite. UV printer koristimo najčešće za izradu grafika prezentacijskih sustava, banner te naljepnica.
Seiko H-104s

Seiko H-104s je mild solventni ink-jet printer dizajniran da pruži vrhunske performance uz nisku cijenu ispisa. Solvent tisak karakterizira trajnost ispisa, otpornost na vanjske uvjete (kiša, sunce, vjetar) te otpornost na mehanička oštećenja (grebanje).

Koristi se u izradi Jumbo plakata, PVC naljepnica, backlit i frontlit bannera, plakata, prozorske grafike. Negativna strana solventnog tiska je miris. Potrebno nekoliko dana se print osuši te da miris u potpunosti nestane, pa stoga nije idealan za unutarnje prostore.

content.text: The Kapa board is a lightweight board filled with polyurethane foam.
It is intended exclusively for indoor spaces and is most often used for pictures, presentation signs, interior advertising on walls, hangers from ceilings, etc.
The boards are very suitable for cutting (shaping) and are extremely lightweight.
We do the imaging with direct UV print on the board or with digital solvent or UV print on a sticker, which we then mount onto a kappa board.
We also offer contour cutting, i.e. making the desired shape and format.
Materials:
Kapa Line
- A lightweight board covered on both sides with white paper, filled with polyurethane foam, ideal for screen printing, application and model-making.
Kapa Plast

- A sandwich board filled with waterproof foam, covered with a mixture of plastic and cellulose in white, which makes it resistant to moisture. It is used for screen printing, signs from coloured self-adhesive film, poster mounting, etc.
Kapa Fix
- A sandwich board with a self-adhesive layer, for mounting posters. Under the layer a thin sheet of aluminium foil is applied, which enables mounting of larger formats.
Kapa Mount
- A board identical in structure to the Kapa Fix board, but without the self-adhesive layer, which makes it ideal for mounting posters printed on self-adhesive films
Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).

content.text: A poster is a printed promotional material most often used in promoting various products, services, advertising new products or various events such as a concert, exhibition, fair, event...

The standard poster sizes are: A3 (29.7x42cm), B2 (50x70cm), B1 (70x100cm), but we also make them in various other dimensions according to your wishes.
Depending on quantity, posters are printed in offset or digital print.
Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
Offset printing

Offset printing is a printing technique in which the print is transferred from the offset plate to a rubber blanket, and then onto a sheet of paper. It is an indirect process of reproducing the printing form onto the printing substrate.
The greatest advantage of offset printing is the top print quality and a very favourable price for larger print runs.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).

content.text: PVC self-adhesive films are most often used for wrapping vehicles, decorating interiors or exteriors of spaces, for fairs, marking, etc.
Along with printing, we also offer contour cutting, i.e. making stickers of the desired shape and format.
It is possible to print on white or transparent PVC film, with a glossy or matte effect, and it can additionally be protected with lamination.
Such PVC stickers are resistant to all atmospheric or climatic conditions, so they are most often used for outdoor conditions.
For making self-adhesive stickers we use only top-quality and durable materials.
Depending on your wishes, our standard range includes the following materials:
Monomeric film
intended for application to flat surfaces. Film durability up to 4 years.
Polymeric film
for application to flat and slightly curved surfaces. Film durability up to 7 years.
Cast film
is a thin and extremely stretchable film with permanent adhesive intended for application to highly curved surfaces (vehicles). Film durability 7 years.
Translucent film
is a translucent film for use in illuminated displays. Film durability up to 7 years
Easy Dot film
and with dot adhesive for easier handling, repositioning and installation. Durability up to 2 years.
Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).

content.text: The Forex board is a board made of foam PVC. It is distinguished by low weight and good hardness.
As a material it is suitable for shaping advertising or presentation structures, information boards; it enables quality direct printing, mounting and lamination.
Suitable for indoor and outdoor use.
The boards are very suitable for cutting (shaping) and are extremely lightweight.

We do the imaging with direct UV print on the board or with digital solvent or UV print on a sticker, which we then mount onto a forex board. We also offer contour cutting, i.e. making the desired shape and format.
Forex comes in thicknesses of 1mm, 2mm, 3mm, 4mm, 5mm, 10mm and in various colours shown in the image.
Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
Nocai UL 600
Nocai UL 600 is the latest technique of direct printing on various types of flat products and slightly curved/relief substrates.
Its greatest advantage is that, in addition to the basic colours, it can print with white ink and UV varnish.
With multiple layers of ink a relief print can be achieved. The work table size is 70x90cm and 60cm high.
VHF Active Pro CNC
With the VHF Active Pro CNC (computer numerical control) machine we cut the shape (of text or graphics) on a flat-surface substrate using a computer-guided machine.
Engraving is performed using a milling cutter attached to an electric motor mounted on the carrying bridge, and the machine's work table size is 200x300cm.
Materials that can be cut include forex, alubond, wood, aluminium, accafoam, plexi, etc.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).

content.text: Window graphics or One Way Vision sticker is a PVC film which, when applied to glass, has the visual effect that from the outside the printed graphic is seen, while from the inside looking out it appears as if there is no film on the glass at all, thus preventing unwanted views into shop windows and vehicles, while providing the possibility of an advertising message.
It is most often applied to various glass surfaces, shop windows, offices, vehicles, etc.

Window graphics or One Way Vision sticker is a PVC film which, when applied to glass, has the visual effect that from the outside the printed graphic is seen, while from the inside looking out it appears as if there is no film on the glass at all.
Window graphics can be used on any glass or window, such as shop windows, car windows, buses and other vehicles, office windows, displays and the like.
These films significantly reduce UV radiation and sunlight, which is particularly useful if the office is exposed to the sun.
For making self-adhesive stickers we use only top-quality and durable materials.
Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).

content.text: The Roll-up Roti is a new form of the most popular solution for presenting your company, products and services. The Roll-up is ideal for presentation at various occasions due to its easy and simple assembly and simple transport. This stand is the best choice for clients who expect a high-quality product and graphics that are always protected during transport.

The Roll-up is ideal for presentation at various occasions due to its easy and simple assembly and simple transport. This stand is the best choice for clients who expect a high-quality product and graphics that are always protected during transport. Assembly is very simple and fast; you just need to pull out the graphic and base and clip it onto the support pole. Excellent stability is provided by two legs that are set by rotating 90°.
Roll-up Roti Classic is available in dimensions 85x200, 100x200 and 120x200cm.
Roll-up Roti Eco is available in dimensions 85x200, 100x200.

aluminium stand
transport bag with additional reinforcement
cardboard box
Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).
If you are not sure how our presentation systems are assembled, feel free to contact us and we will be glad to help with our advice.

content.text: PVC banners or tarpaulins are the most common form of outdoor advertising due to their durability and cost-effectiveness.
Frontlit is a double-sided laminated PVC material resistant to outdoor weather conditions.
It is intended for illuminating printed graphics at night from the front.
PVC banners or tarpaulins are the most common form of outdoor advertising due to their durability and cost-effectiveness.
Frontlit is a double-sided laminated PVC material resistant to outdoor weather conditions.
It is intended for illuminating printed graphics at night from the front.
We make all banners with digital solvent or UV print on top-quality and durable material and offer various finishes depending on your needs.
Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).

Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).
If you are not sure how our presentation systems are assembled, feel free to contact us and we will be glad to help with our advice.

hr.shortDescription: Izrada i tisak na Tekstilni Pop-Up zid

content.text: Shirts are the most widespread and most popular promotional article, whether it is a classic T-shirt, an elegant polo or a sports shirt, it is a garment with which you can never go wrong.
We offer a wide selection of shirts to satisfy all customers' wishes (men's or women's, fitted or classic, a wide palette of colours, sleeve lengths…)
Printing on shirts is most often done using screen printing and DTF.
It is possible to print on shirts in one or more colours, on almost all types of shirts, polo shirts or other types and weights of shirts.
In addition to screen printing, we can also offer machine embroidery (stitch) or direct printing on textile.
DTF print

DTG digital printing is a new technology that applies the printed motif directly onto the article via a film, and during production the ink is partly absorbed into the structure of the fabric itself, so the imprint is much softer to the touch and more comfortable to wear than imprints made by some other techniques.

DTF digital printing is done by first applying the motif to special films and then transferring it onto the article using a heat press. Due to this production method, it can — apart from cotton and cotton-polyester blends — be applied to almost all types of fabrics and materials: polyester (jerseys, shirts, bags), softshell, jeans, faux leather, leather (wallets, planners, bags), wood, etc.
Screen printing

Screen printing is the oldest printing technique with a wide application, especially for finished advertising or printed products. It is used for printing on various materials, e.g. printing on textile, metal, PVC substrates, ceramics, rubber or various promotional articles.
Screen printing is distinguished by a long imprint lifespan in all conditions of use and high coverage, so that a quality screen print has many years of use without damage.
Machine embroidery or stitch
Machine embroidery or stitch is distinguished by excellent quality and durability, a wide choice of thread colours of high strength and colourfastness.
Machine embroidery is suitable for application to various types of textile materials, especially materials that cannot withstand thermal application.

hr.name: Majice kratkih rukava

content.text: Tisak na majice se najčešće izrađuje tehnikom sitotiska i DTF-om.
Moguće je tiskati na majice u jednoj ili više boja, na skoro sve vrste majica, polo majica ili nekih drugih vrsta i gramatura majica.
Osim sitotiska, možemo ponuditi i strojni vez (štik) ili direktni tisak na tekstil.
DTF tisak

DTG digitalni tisak nova je tehnologija koja isprintani motiv aplicira direktno na artikl putem filma, a prilikom izrade boja se djelomično upija u strukturu same tkanine pa je otisak na opip puno mekši i ugodniji za nošenje od otisaka napravljenih nekim drugim tehnikama.

DTF digitalni tisak izrađuje se na način da se motiv prvo aplicira na specijalne folije pa onda pomoću termo preše prenosi na artikl. Zbog ovakvog načina izrade isti se, osim na pamuk i mješavine pamuk-poliester, može aplicirati na gotovo sve vrste tkanina i materijala: polyester (dresovi, majice, torbe), softshell, jeans, skaj, koža (novčanici, rokovnici, torbe), drvo itd.
Sitotisak

Sitotisak je najstarija tehnika tiska koja ima široku primjenu, posebno kod gotovih reklamnih ili tiskanih proizvoda.
Koristi za tisak na razne materijale kao npr. tisak na tekstil, metal, PVC podloge, keramiku, gumu ili različite promotivne artikle.
Sitotisak odlikuje dugi vijek trajanja otiska u svim uvjetima korištenja i velika pokrivnost, tako da kvalitetno izvedene tisak u sitotisku ima višegodišnju upotrebu bez oštećenja.
Strojni vez ili štik
Strojni vez ili štik se odlikuje odličnom kvalitetom i trajnošću, veliki izbor boja konca visoke čvrstoće i postojanosti.
Strojni vez je pogodan za apliciranje na razne vrste tekstilnih materijala, specijalno na materijale koji ne podnose termo apliciranje.

U ponudi imamo široki izbor majica kako bi zadovoljili sve želje kupaca (muške ili ženske, strukirane ili klasične, široka paleta boja, dužina rukava…)

Mimaki UJV 55-320
We are able to print at a maximum width of 320cm at a speed of 177m2/h. The Mimaki UJV55-320 is a large-format printer with a maximum print width of 320cm.

It enables high imprint quality, fast printing and cost-effectiveness, and the main advantage of the UV printer is that there is no need to laminate the imprint for protection. We use the UV printer most often for making graphics for presentation systems, banners and stickers.
Seiko H-104s

The Seiko H-104s is a mild-solvent ink-jet printer designed to deliver top performance at a low printing cost. Solvent printing is characterised by imprint durability, resistance to outdoor conditions (rain, sun, wind) and resistance to mechanical damage (scratching).

It is used in making Jumbo posters, PVC stickers, backlit and frontlit banners, posters, window graphics. The downside of solvent printing is the smell. It takes a few days for the print to dry and for the smell to disappear completely, so it is not ideal for indoor spaces.
When creating artwork, there are a few things you should keep in mind in order to create correct artwork, so we have put together a few tips and guidelines.
If you are not sure how best to prepare a document for our printing, feel free to call us on 098 9085 552 and we will gladly help with our advice.
Colours and gradients in the file

Prepare the supplied files using CMYK colours, never RGB, and if within your document you use colours that are not CMYK but RGB they will be converted to CMYK, in which case minor or major deviations in the fidelity of colour reproduction are possible, for which we accept no responsibility.
Avoid 4C for black; instead it is sufficient that it is 100% K (black).
When using special colours (Pantone or HKS) please note this specifically when ordering.
Check that all overlapping objects are set correctly (overprint).
If you order a file in grey, we recommend that the grey be created in shades of black.
White must be a separate spot colour, with the mandatory name “White_Ink“ (mind upper and lower case), in overprint and in the top layer.

For black areas, 100% black is not enough to obtain a stronger and darker black. For richness of black, use a CMYK colour consisting of: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. This does not apply to files intended for printing on textile, i.e. by sublimation; then the black must be C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

For making a verlauf (transition, gradient) we recommend that you make it within Photoshop, because vector-generated gradients have problems during RIPping and "steps" often appear across the gradient range (to be completely sure we have avoided the possibility of steps, it is good to apply an "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) to the gradient).
File size, bleed and margins
Create the files at their actual final dimensions with bleed.
Enlarging a smaller file format to a larger format can lead to a reduction in resolution quality. For example, enlarging an A6 leaflet to an A4 leaflet can affect the quality of your final product.

Always add bleed to the final file dimension, because this will make cutting to format easier and no white border will appear. The bleed should be 3mm over the edge of the finished format unless otherwise defined in the artwork-preparation instructions for that product.
Bleed is defined for all four sides regardless of the page position (left, right) and the type of binding.
Pages are sent individually, centred on the output format. There can be several in one document, but only with crop marks; all other marks are superfluous.
All content should be at least 5mm from the cut line; for some products a safe zone is defined (pink line)
For background colours or images, if they go to the edge of the product, leave a bleed.
Images, graphics, text and lines
All raster elements of the artwork should be around:
30 dpi for XXL formats over 12 m2 (jumbo posters, megaboards…),
60 to 100 dpi for A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 formats (posters, prints, counters, roll ups, banners…),
100 to 150 dpi for A3 format (smaller posters, images…),
200 to 300 dpi for A4, A5 formats (catalogues, brochures, business cards…).
Logos, text, lines, etc. should be in vector format
If the artwork contains text, convert all text to curves or send the font used for PC.

Files should be at a 1:1 ratio for smaller visuals or 1:10 for large visuals; if the artwork is not at 1:1 scale, then it is necessary to state at what scale it was made and what the final dimension is.
Lines should be at least 0.125 pt thick

Please adjust the lines so they are visible when printed; depending on the material being produced, the thickness should be adjusted accordingly - greater thickness on flags, while a thinner line on a leaflet.
File format
We prefer documents to be supplied in pdf or tif format. We also accept the following file formats for digital printing: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Along with the artwork file, please also send a lower-resolution preview (.jpg).
If you are not sure how our presentation systems are assembled, feel free to contact us and we will be glad to help with our advice.

Boje i gradijenti u datoteci

Dostavljene datoteke pripremite koristeći CMYK boje, a nikako RGB, a ako unutar vašeg dokumenta koristite boje koje nisu CMYK nego RGB one će biti konvertirani u CMYK prilikom čega su mogući manji ili veći odmaci u vjernosti reprodukcije boja i za što nepreuzimamo odgovornost.
Izbjegavajte 4C za crnu boju; umjesto toga dovoljno je da je 100% K (crna).
Kada koristite specijalne boje (Pantone ili HKS) molimo vas da posebno napomenete kod narudžbe.
Provjerite da li su svi objekti koji se preklapaju ispravno podešeni (overprint).
Ako naručite datoteku u sivoj boji, tada preporučujemo da je siva stvorena u nijansama crne.
Bijela boja mora biti zasebna spot boja, obaveznog naziva “White_Ink“ (paziti na velika i mala slova), u overprintu i u top layeru.

Kod crnih ploha, 100% crna boja nije dovoljna da bi dobili jaču i tamniju crnu boju. Za punoću crne boje koristite CMYK boju koji se sastoji od: C: 40% ; M: 40% ; Y: 40% ; K: 100%. Ovo ne vrijedi za datoteke namijenjene za print na tekstil, odnosno sublimacijom, tada mora biti crna C: 0% ; M: 0% ; Y: 0% ; K: 100%.

Za izradu verlauf (prijelaz, gradijent) preporučujemo da ga napravite unutar Photoshop-a jer vektorski generirani gradijenti imaju problema prilikom RIP-anja i često dolazi do pojave “stepenica” u rasponu gradijenta (kako bi bili potpuno sigurni da smo izbjegli mogućnost stepenica dobro je napraviti "Add noise" filter (max. 2-3) na gradijentu).
Veličina, napusti i margine datoteke
Datoteke kreirajte u njihovoj stvarnoj konačnoj dimenziji sa napustima.
Povećanje manjeg formata datoteke na veći format može dovesti do smanjenja kvalitete razlučivosti. Na primjer, povećanje A6 letka na letak A4, može utjecati na kvalitetu vašeg konačog proizvoda.

Uvijek dodajte napust (bleed) na konačnu dimenziju datoteke jer ćete time olakšati kod rezanja na format i neće se pojavljivati bijeli obrub Napust neka iznosi 3mm preko ruba završenog formata osim ako nije drugačije definirano u uputi za grafičku priprema za taj proizvod.
Napusti se definiraju za sve četiri strane bez obzira na poziciju stranice (lijeva, desna), te vrstu uveza.
Stranice se šalju pojedinačno centrirane na izlazni format Može ih biti i više u jednom dokumentu, ali samo s oznakama reza, sve ostale oznake su suvišne.
Sav sadržaj treba biti barem 5mm od linije reza; kod nekih proizvoda je definirana sigurna zona (roza linija)
Kod pozadinskih boja ili slika, ukoliko idu do ruba proizvoda, tada ostavite napust.
Slike, grafike, tekst i linije
Svi rasterski elementi grafičke pripreme trebali bi biti oko:
30 dpi za XXL formate preko 12 m2 (jumbo plakati, megaboardi…),
60 do 100 dpi za formate A0, A1, B0, B1, B2 (plakati, posteri, pultevi, roll upovi, banneri…),
100 do 150 dpi za format A3 (manji plakati, slike…),
200 do 300 dpi za formate A4, A5 (katalozi, prospekti, vizitke…).
Logotipovi, tekstovi, linije i sl. trebaju biti u vektorskom obliku
Ako priprema sadrži tekst, sav tekst pretvoriti u krivulje ili poslati korišteni font za PC.

Datoteke neka budu u omjeru 1:1 za manje vizuale ili 1:10 za velike vizuale; ukoliko priprema nije u 1:1 mjerilu, tada je potrebno naglasiti u kojem je mjerilu napravljena i koja je finalna dimenzija.
Linije trebaju biti debljine barem 0.125 pt
Molimo da linije prilagodite tako da budu vidljive kod tiska; ovisno na kojem materijalu se izrađuje shodno treba i podesiti debljinu-na zastavama veća debljina dok na letku tanja linija.
Format datoteke
Preferiramo dostavu dokumenata u pdf ili tif formatu. Prihvaćamo i slijedeće formate datoteka za digitalni tisak: .JPG, EPS, .AI, .PSD, .CDR
Uz datoteku s grafičkom pripremom, molimo pošaljite i preview niže rezolucije (.jpg).
